subject: physics

moments.title: Fourier's heat equation
moments.body: Fourier's 'Théorie analytique de la chaleur' includes the diffusion equation for heat flow — q = -k dT/dx. The equation generalises to all diffusion processes.
moments.takeaway: Heat conduction obeys a partial differential equation.

moments.title: Kelvin's age of Earth
moments.body: Kelvin uses Fourier's heat equation to calculate how long Earth has been cooling from a molten state. His answer: 20-400 million years. This contradicts Darwin's biology and Lyell's geology, which demand hundreds of millions or billions of years.
moments.takeaway: Heat conduction is used to attack evolutionary biology.

moments.title: Curies measure radium's heat
moments.body: Radium continuously generates heat — a previously unknown energy source. Rutherford realises radioactive heating inside Earth invalidates Kelvin's calculation; Earth can be much older.
moments.takeaway: Kelvin's argument collapses; Earth is 4.5 billion years old.

moments.title: Earth's age measured
moments.body: Patterson dates meteorites with uranium-lead chronology and gets 4.55 ± 0.07 billion years. The biologists were right; Kelvin was wrong.
moments.takeaway: Radioactivity solves the age-of-Earth controversy in the geologists' favour.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Earth is 4.54 billion years old. Heat conduction equations describe thermal management in CPUs, building insulation, planetary interiors and stellar atmospheres.
now.open_questions: How much of Earth's interior heat is primordial vs radiogenic?

reflection: Kelvin was a giant who used impeccable thermodynamics — and was wrong. What does that say about confidence in our own current best models?
